title: Work Participation of Informal Caregivers of Cancer Patients—Barriers, Enabling Factors, and Support Needs
summary:
Background: The rising number of cancer cases and the increasing shift toward home-based care mean that family members and other close associates (informal caregivers) are increasingly taking on caregiving responsibilities. These caregiving responsibilities can lead to physical, psychological, and occupational stress, particularly when combined with paid employment. To date, it remains unclear to what extent caregiving responsibilities can be reconciled with the paid employment of family members or other close associates who serve as informal caregivers. 

Research question: This project therefore aims to examine the effects of taking on caregiving responsibilities on the informal carers’ work participation. In particular, the project aims to identify barriers, facilitating factors, and support needs related to their work participation. 

Methodology: Focus groups with informal caregivers will be conducted and evaluated using thematic analysis.
conditions: Informal caregivers of an adult cancer patient

interventions.name: Caregivers participate in a one-time focus group discussion and complete a short questionnaire

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The person:
- identifies as an informal caregiver for an adult with cancer who is currently undergoing treatment for cancer or has undergone treatment for cancer within the past five years; 
- is currently employed or was employed during the period of caregiving; 
- has sufficient proficiency in German to participate in discussions.
Exclusion criteria:
Participants will be excluded if they have health limitations that prevent them from participating in the focus group and/or if their German language skills are insufficient to allow them to participate in the discussion.
